bougie:Restaurant 360 — Adriatic-meets-A.name: Restaurant 360 — Adriatic-meets-Asia tasting menu
bougie:Restaurant 360 — Adriatic-meets-A.label: WALL-TOP
bougie:Restaurant 360 — Adriatic-meets-A.text: The ★-since-2018 tasting menu inside the arches above the Old Port. Chef Marijo Curić's line is Mediterranean technique with Asian ferments and French sauce-work. Closed November to late March; reopens 27 March 2026. EUR 230–280 menu; book 2–3 months ahead. Sunset table on the terrace is the request. Where Old Town · Sv. Dominika bb

bougie:Nautika — anniversary dinner at P.name: Nautika — anniversary dinner at Pile
bougie:Nautika — anniversary dinner at P.label: CLASSIC LUXURY
bougie:Nautika — anniversary dinner at P.text: Set in the former Nautical School (1881) with the terrace over Kolorina Bay between Bokar and Lovrijenac. Chef Mario Bunda runs the conservative classic-luxury kitchen: lobster bisque, whole turbot for two, soufflé glacé Grand Marnier. The room is the experience. EUR 120–180 pp. Book 2+ weeks for the sea-side terrace; sunset table. Where Pile · Brsalje 3

bougie:Stara Loža — 16-seat rooftop.name: Stara Loža — 16-seat rooftop
bougie:Stara Loža — 16-seat rooftop.label: ROOFTOP
bougie:Stara Loža — 16-seat rooftop.text: The one Prijeko Street address that is not a trap. Three spaces stacked vertically; the 16-seat rooftop is the request. Chef's day-market menu — sea bass in salt crust, oysters from Ston in season, scampi linguine. Michelin Guide listed continuously since 2017. Book 3+ weeks. EUR 80–140 pp. Where Old Town · Prijeko 22

dish:Šporki makaruli.name: Šporki makaruli
dish:Šporki makaruli.label: FEAST-DAY
dish:Šporki makaruli.hook: Hand-cut pasta in a slow beef ragù — the "dirty macaroni" of the patrician table
chips: Lunch / dinner, Jan 31 – Feb 4 most authentically
dish:Šporki makaruli.text: Hand-cut pasta in a slow beef ragù — the "dirty macaroni" of the patrician table EUR 15–25 FEAST-DAY Lunch / dinner, Jan 31 – Feb 4 most authentically Hand-cut macaroni in a deep slow-cooked beef and veal ragù with bay and cloves, traditionally served on or around St Blaise Day (3 February) . Across the 31 Jan – 4 Feb week ~19 Old Town kitchens run a unified šporki menu — tzdubrovnik.hr publishes the participating list. The name means literally "dirty macaroni": patrician households ate the meat from the ragù, then poured what was left over pasta for the servants on feast days — late-comers got progressively less sauce, hence "dirtier" plates. The city kept the recipe and let go of the hierarchy. Best at Kopun . Where Old Town · St Blaise Day 3 Feb

dish:Pašticada.name: Pašticada
dish:Pašticada.label: BRAISED
dish:Pašticada.hook: Beef larded with cloves, marinated 24–48 h in Prošek, braised 4–6 h, served with njoki
dish:Pašticada.text: Beef larded with cloves, marinated 24–48 h in Prošek, braised 4–6 h, served with njoki EUR 22–35 EVERYWHERE Lunch or dinner; a 2-day dish Beef topside or rump, larded with pancetta, garlic and cloves, marinated 24–48 hours in vinegar and Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert wine, not Italian Prosecco (the EU-PDO fight that Croatia partially lost in 2022). Then braised four to six hours with prunes, dried figs, root vegetables, bay, peppercorns and cinnamon. Always served with njoki (gnocchi) . The sauce comes out sweet-sour and unmistakable. A two-day dish at minimum — call ahead to confirm a restaurant has it on; the best versions are at home or at the konobas. Where Dalmatian-wide, Dubrovnik canonical

dish:Mali Ston oysters — Ostrea edulis.name: Mali Ston oysters — Ostrea edulis
dish:Mali Ston oysters — Ostrea edulis.label: PDO 2020
dish:Mali Ston oysters — Ostrea edulis.hook: European flat oyster · only farmed Ostrea edulis PDO in Europe · peak Mar–May
chips: Late morning to early afternoon — off the boat
dish:Mali Ston oysters — Ostrea edulis.text: European flat oyster · only farmed Ostrea edulis PDO in Europe · peak Mar–May EUR 2.50–4 / oyster AT SOURCE Late morning to early afternoon — off the boat The European flat oyster (Ostrea edulis), the noble flat — not the cupped Pacific. Farmed in Mali Ston Bay since Roman times — Pliny the Elder mentioned them. EU PDO registered by Commission Implementing Regulation 2020/1469 of 6 October 2020 — the only farmed Ostrea edulis PDO in Europe and ~90% of Croatian oyster production. Peak season is March to May ; the traditional opening day is St Joseph (19 March) . ~140–200 tons a year. Eat them raw with lemon at the boat at Bota Šare with a glass of Pošip — Old Town versions are 1 h 30 by road and may be three days old by the time they reach a plate inside the walls. Where Mali Ston Bay · Pelješac

dish:Crni rižot.name: Crni rižot
dish:Crni rižot.label: INK
dish:Crni rižot.hook: Black risotto with cuttlefish — independent Adriatic tradition, not a Venetian copy
dish:Crni rižot.text: Black risotto with cuttlefish — independent Adriatic tradition, not a Venetian copy EUR 18–28 EVERYWHERE Lunch or dinner Dalmatian black risotto with cuttlefish (or squid / octopus) and its ink — tomato base, white wine, garlic, parsley; ink stirred in 60–90 seconds before service so the rice stays slick and the colour stays mat-black, not muddy. Independent of the Venetian risotto al nero — the Adriatic tradition runs both shores and Dalmatia kept it through Ragusan independence. Best paired with a Pošip from Korčula. Reliable versions at Proto , Kopun , Bota Šare . Where Dalmatian-wide

dish:Janjetina ispod peke.name: Janjetina ispod peke
dish:Janjetina ispod peke.label: UNDER THE BELL
dish:Janjetina ispod peke.hook: Lamb cooked 3 hours under the iron bell — order ahead
dish:Janjetina ispod peke.text: Lamb cooked 3 hours under the iron bell — order ahead EUR 30–55 / kg PRE-ORDER Long lunch or early dinner Janjetina ispod peke — lamb (or veal, or octopus) cooked under the iron bell on a wood-ember hearth for three hours with potatoes, rosemary, olive oil. Or janjetina s ražnja : whole lamb on a spit, salted only, over open fire for 4–5 h. The countryside version of the Sunday roast. Call by 14:00 for an evening peka , by 11:00 for lunch. The bell is the original slow oven: heat from above and below, no opening till service. Best at Konoba Dubrava above the city, or at Konoba Konavoski Komin south. Where Konavle · Bosanka · countryside

dish:Brodet / brudet.name: Brodet / brudet
dish:Brodet / brudet.label: STEW
dish:Brodet / brudet.hook: Fisherman's stew with at least three species — never stirred, always shaken
dish:Brodet / brudet.text: Fisherman's stew with at least three species — never stirred, always shaken EUR 18–30 EVERYWHERE Lunch or dinner Fisherman's stew: at least three Adriatic species (grouper, scorpionfish, eel, monkfish, sea bream, John Dory) — tomato, onion, garlic, paprika, a glass of red (usually Plavac Mali, the local paradox of red wine in fish stew). Never stirred — shaken : the pan is rotated and tilted so the fish stays whole. Served with polenta or boiled potato. The Konavle freshwater variant uses river fish or — at Konavoski Dvori — frog. The dish that turns by-catch into the day's headline. Where Coastal Dalmatia

dish:Zelena menestra.name: Zelena menestra
dish:Zelena menestra.label: WINTER
dish:Zelena menestra.hook: Green winter stew — cabbage, smoked pork, kaštradina — documented since 1480
dish:Zelena menestra.text: Green winter stew — cabbage, smoked pork, kaštradina — documented since 1480 EUR 14–22 WINTER Lunch or supper, Nov–Mar Dubrovnik's winter green stew — collard or kale or Savoy cabbage simmered in smoked-pork broth with kaštradina (dried sheep or lamb), sausage and potato. Documented in Dubrovnik writings as early as 1480 . Three regional sub-versions: City, Župska, Primorska. The centerpiece of Konavle Christmas tables. The kaštradina is the key — air-dried mountain mutton, rare to find outside Dalmatia; ask any Konavle agroturizam if they can hold a leg. Where City · Župa · Primorska

drink:Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfan.name: Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfandel
drink:Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfan.label: RED
drink:Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfan.hook: Native red of Pelješac · Crljenak × Dobričić · UC Davis 1998 DNA proof
chips: Dinner, paired with brodet or peka
drink:Plavac Mali — grandchild of Zinfan.text: Native red of Pelješac · Crljenak × Dobričić · UC Davis 1998 DNA proof EUR 18–120 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner, paired with brodet or peka "Little blue" — the native red of Dalmatia. Prof. Carole Meredith at UC Davis in 1998 , with vine cuttings shipped by Mike Grgich himself, proved that Plavac Mali is the offspring of Crljenak Kaštelanski × Dobričić — and that Crljenak Kaštelanski is genetically identical to Zinfandel (California) and Primitivo (Apulia). So Croatia is the grandparent of California Zinfandel. The flagship appellations: Dingač (1961) and Postup (1967), both on Pelješac's south-facing slopes. Where Pelješac peninsula

drink:Dingač — Croatia's first protected.name: Dingač — Croatia's first protected wine
drink:Dingač — Croatia's first protected.label: APPELLATION 1961
drink:Dingač — Croatia's first protected.hook: 1961 appellation · 45° slopes · grapes sun-cooked three times
drink:Dingač — Croatia's first protected.text: 1961 appellation · 45° slopes · grapes sun-cooked three times EUR 28–80 / bottle ESSENTIAL Dinner Dingač was declared in 1961 — the first protected wine appellation in former Yugoslavia and modern Croatia. The vines grow on south-facing 45° slopes between Trstenik and Podobuče on the Pelješac peninsula, where the grapes are heat-cooked three ways at once: direct sun, sun reflected off the Adriatic, sun reflected off the white karst stones. Historically the grapes were brought down by donkey through a hand-dug path; since 1973 the ~400 m Dingač tunnel connects Potomje on the cooler north shore to the warm south. Drink at D'vino in a flight if you can't make Pelješac. Where Pelješac · Trstenik–Podobuče

drink:Pošip — Korčula white.name: Pošip — Korčula white
drink:Pošip — Korčula white.label: WHITE
drink:Pošip — Korčula white.hook: Native white of Korčula · first documented 1864 · first protected Croatian white (PGI 1967)
drink:Pošip — Korčula white.text: Native white of Korčula · first documented 1864 · first protected Croatian white (PGI 1967) EUR 14–55 / bottle ESSENTIAL Lunch with oysters; aperitivo Pošip is the white that pairs with Mali Ston oysters. Native to Korčula, grown almost exclusively in the Smokvičko-čarsko polje — the linked vineyards of Smokvica and Čara . First documented vine 1864 (Marin Tomašić of Čara); PGI status in 1967, the first protected white wine in Croatia . DNA work shows the grape is a natural cross of Bratovina × Blatska Zlatarica. Notes: citrus, salt, almond, the mouthfeel of a lower-acid Mediterranean white. Usually 13.5–14.5% abv. Try Krajančić , Bire , Toreta , or the Grgić Pošip. Where Korčula · Smokvica · Čara

drink:Grk — only Lumbarda.name: Grk — only Lumbarda
drink:Grk — only Lumbarda.label: SINGLE-VILLAGE
drink:Grk — only Lumbarda.hook: Single-village white from sandy soils · ~2,400 years on the island · female-only vines
drink:Grk — only Lumbarda.text: Single-village white from sandy soils · ~2,400 years on the island · female-only vines EUR 22–48 / bottle RARE Aperitivo or with crudo "The Greek" — white wine from a single village, Lumbarda on the eastern tip of Korčula. Planted by Greek colonists from Issa (Vis) in the 4th c. BCE . Grown in sandy soils that resisted phylloxera , which is why the vines are pre-phylloxera ungrafted. The genetic curiosity: Grk vines are female-only and must be co-planted with Plavac Mali to set fruit. Production is small — under 100 ha in total — and a chef can drink it nowhere in the Old Town except D'vino , who stocks the Bire and Lumbarda Vina bottlings. Where Korčula · Lumbarda

drink:Maraschino — Dominican friars, 16t.name: Maraschino — Dominican friars, 16th c.
drink:Maraschino — Dominican friars, 16t.label: LIQUEUR
drink:Maraschino — Dominican friars, 16t.hook: Clear cherry liqueur from the Marasca cherry · perfected by Dominican monks · on the Titanic
drink:Maraschino — Dominican friars, 16t.text: Clear cherry liqueur from the Marasca cherry · perfected by Dominican monks · on the Titanic EUR 3–6 / pour EVERYWHERE Aperitivo or digestif Clear cherry liqueur from the Marasca cherry of the Zadar hinterland. Brought from Asia Minor in Roman times; Dominican friars in Zadar perfected the liqueur in the 16th century ; the Venetian merchant Francesco Drioli industrialized production in 1759 . Maraska d.d. (founded 1946) consolidated the Zadar producers post-war. The liqueur was on the first-class drinks list of the Titanic in 1912. The right move at home: dry maraschino in an old fashioned with Plavac-Mali syrup, or float on top of a champagne cup. Where Zadar hinterland — Dalmatian-wide

drink:Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Roza.name: Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Rozalin
drink:Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Roza.label: RAKIJA
drink:Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Roza.hook: Herb / grape / walnut / rose-petal — the home rakija quartet
drink:Travarica · Loza · Orahovac · Roza.text: Herb / grape / walnut / rose-petal — the home rakija quartet EUR 3–6 / pour EVERYWHERE Aperitivo and digestif Travarica — clear grape rakija infused with sage, rosemary, fennel and immortelle; the aperitivo. Loza — the straight grape eau-de-vie of the coast. Orahovac — green-walnut liqueur: walnuts picked unripe around St John's Day, 24 June , steeped 40+ days in rakija with cloves, cinnamon and sugar — comes out dark amber and tastes Christmas-y. Rozalin / Rozulin — Dubrovnik-specific rose-petal liqueur, the perfume that makes a proper Rožata caramel taste of Dubrovnik and not of crème caramel elsewhere. Where Konavle agroturizam · home tables

drink:Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert win.name: Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert wine
drink:Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert win.label: DESSERT WINE
drink:Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert win.hook: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine — name fight with Italian Prosecco (partially lost 2022)
chips: With dessert; a hit of it in pašticada marinade
drink:Prošek — the Dalmatian dessert win.text: Sun-dried-grape dessert wine — name fight with Italian Prosecco (partially lost 2022) EUR 18–60 / bottle ESSENTIAL FOR PAŠTICADA With dessert; a hit of it in pašticada marinade Prošek is the Dalmatian dessert wine — grapes sun-dried on straw mats for 2–3 weeks to concentrate sugars, then fermented slowly. Sweet, port-like, amber. Not Italian Prosecco : the Italian sparkling shares only the syllable. The EU-PDO arbitration of 2022 partially rejected Croatia's Prošek protection in favour of Italian Prosecco — a sore point on every Dalmatian dinner table. The dessert wine still gets called Prošek inside Croatia; it is also the soul of pašticada's marinade. Try Hectorovich from Hvar or Saints Hills Prošek . Where Dalmatian-wide

music:Oliver Dragojević — \"Cesarica\".name: Oliver Dragojević — "Cesarica"
music:Oliver Dragojević — \"Cesarica\".label: DALMATIAN VOICE
music:Oliver Dragojević — \"Cesarica\".hook: The Dalmatian voice — "Cesarica" (1993, written by Gibonni) is the regional anthem
music:Oliver Dragojević — \"Cesarica\".text: The Dalmatian voice — "Cesarica" (1993, written by Gibonni) is the regional anthem The defining post-war voice of Dalmatia. Born in Vela Luka on Korčula in 1947, died 29 July 2018. The funeral procession from Split to Vela Luka was hundreds of boats. "Cesarica" (1993, written for Oliver by Gibonni) is the song every Dalmatian knows from the first three bars. Albums to queue while prepping service: Vridilo je (2009), Pjesma o ljubavi , anything from the 1980s with the brass section. Klapa-rooted but with a smoky jazz shadow. Where Vela Luka, Korčula (b. 7 Dec 1947 – d. 29 Jul 2018)

music:Gibonni — 43 Porin awards.name: Gibonni — 43 Porin awards
music:Gibonni — 43 Porin awards.label: RECORD-HOLDER
music:Gibonni — 43 Porin awards.hook: Klapa-rooted pop · wrote Cesarica for Oliver · the most-awarded Croatian artist
music:Gibonni — 43 Porin awards.text: Klapa-rooted pop · wrote Cesarica for Oliver · the most-awarded Croatian artist Zlatan Stipišić Gibonni, born Split 13 August 1968. Croatia's most-awarded artist with 43 Porin awards . Songwriter and singer; the bridge between klapa tradition and modern pop. Tracks worth queuing: "Libar" , "Činim pravu stvar" , "Tek je 12 sati" . He wrote Cesarica for Oliver in 1993 — the two names anchor any Dalmatian playlist. Live at the Pula Arena every summer; check the Dubrovnik Summer Festival for an occasional appearance. Where Split (b. 13 Aug 1968)

music:Klapa Cambi — five-time Omiš gold.name: Klapa Cambi — five-time Omiš gold
music:Klapa Cambi — five-time Omiš gold.label: KLAPA
music:Klapa Cambi — five-time Omiš gold.hook: Modern klapa at its tightest · UNESCO ICH 2012
music:Klapa Cambi — five-time Omiš gold.text: Modern klapa at its tightest · UNESCO ICH 2012 Klapa is Dalmatian a cappella multipart singing — four to ten male singers in a tight semicircle, first tenor leads, the others stack chords below. UNESCO ICH listed in 2012. Klapa Cambi from Split are five-time gold medalists at the Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa Songs — the national competition. Defining track "Moj lipi anđele" . Also queue: Klapa Iskon ( "Dobra večer prijatelji" ), Klapa Maslina. Where Split-based klapa

music:Doris Dragović — \"Marija Magdalen.name: Doris Dragović — "Marija Magdalena"
music:Doris Dragović — \"Marija Magdalen.label: EUROVISION
music:Doris Dragović — \"Marija Magdalen.hook: Eurovision 1999 4th place · opened the 2025 Dubrovnik Winter Festival
music:Doris Dragović — \"Marija Magdalen.text: Eurovision 1999 4th place · opened the 2025 Dubrovnik Winter Festival Born Split, 16 April 1961. Eurovision 1986 (Yugoslavia) with "Željo moja" and Eurovision 1999 (Croatia) with "Marija Magdalena" , finishing 4th. The big-stage Dalmatian voice with the national hits of the 90s. Opened the 2025 Dubrovnik Winter Festival on Stradun. Queue "Lice od magle", "Dajem ti srce moje", "Tamara". Where Split (b. 16 Apr 1961)

music:Linđo Folklore Ensemble — Lazareti.name: Linđo Folklore Ensemble — Lazareti
music:Linđo Folklore Ensemble — Lazareti.label: FOLK
music:Linđo Folklore Ensemble — Lazareti.hook: Live Linđo with lijerica all summer · UNESCO-related Konavle circle dance
music:Linđo Folklore Ensemble — Lazareti.text: Live Linđo with lijerica all summer · UNESCO-related Konavle circle dance The Konavle circle dance: a dance-master sits and plays the lijerica — a three-string lyre held on the knee — while calling rhymed commands and stamping rhythm with his right foot . The dancers form a wheel around him. Croatia's UNESCO ICH listed dance traditions. The Linđo Folklore Ensemble performs three times a week at Lazareti (the former 16th-c. plague quarantine, now a cultural centre) just outside Ploče Gate, from late May through early October. Where Lazareti (just outside Ploče Gate)

culture:Republic of Ragusa — the one-mon.name: Republic of Ragusa — the one-month Rector
culture:Republic of Ragusa — the one-mon.label: REPUBLIC 1358–1808
culture:Republic of Ragusa — the one-mon.hook: Senate of 45, Rector for one month — a constitution against personal power
culture:Republic of Ragusa — the one-mon.text: Senate of 45, Rector for one month — a constitution against personal power EUR 15 (Rector's Palace + Cultural Museum) OPEN ALL YEAR Late morning Released from Venice by the Treaty of Zadar in 1358 and abolished by Napoleon's Marshal Marmont in 1808 — four and a half centuries of de facto independence. The Senate had 45 patricians over 40 years old, elected for one year by the Major Council (~300 nobles aged 18+); daily government by the seven-member Minor Council; a Rector who served exactly one month and lived locked inside the Rector's Palace during his term, allowed out only on state business. Visit the Rector's Palace (Gothic-Renaissance, rebuilt after gunpowder explosions in 1435 and 1463) and the Sponza Palace (1516–22) — the customs house, mint and intellectual club of the Republic. Where Old Town · Rector's Palace, Sponza Palace

culture:City Walls — Minčeta, Bokar, Lov.name: City Walls — Minčeta, Bokar, Lovrijenac
culture:City Walls — Minčeta, Bokar, Lov.label: 1,940 m · 13TH–17TH C
chips: Early or late — never midday in summer
culture:City Walls — Minčeta, Bokar, Lov.text: Best walked 07:30 or 17:30 · ~1.5 h loop EUR 35 (combined Walls + Lovrijenac) BOOK-AHEAD Early or late — never midday in summer The walls run 1,940 metres around the Old Town. Maximum height 25 m at the Minčeta Tower (1464, circular Renaissance fort by Michelozzo and Juraj Dalmatinac, with 6 m-thick cannon-deflecting walls). Bokar (1461–63, Michelozzo two-storey casemate) juts forward to flank the Pile Gate. Lovrijenac (St Lawrence) — "Dubrovnik's Gibraltar" — stands on a detached 37 m rock outside the western walls, with seaward walls 12 m thick and city-facing walls only 60 cm so the city could collapse it from within if captured. The inscription over its door: Non bene pro toto libertas venditur auro . Walk the loop at 07:30 or between 17:30 and 18:30 — the stone reads 38–42 °C in full sun and there is no shade on the second half. Where Old Town · ring road on stone

culture:1667 earthquake · the Gradić reb.name: 1667 earthquake · the Gradić rebuild
culture:1667 earthquake · the Gradić reb.label: 6 APRIL 1667
culture:1667 earthquake · the Gradić reb.hook: Why every Stradun façade matches: regulation, not aesthetic accident
culture:1667 earthquake · the Gradić reb.text: Why every Stradun façade matches: regulation, not aesthetic accident Free (Stradun + Sponza) WALK Any 6 April 1667, ~08:45. An 8–15 second earthquake estimated at magnitude ~7 (intensity X EMS) flattened most of the medieval city. ~2,000 died inside the walls per Robin Harris's count (older sources cite up to 5,000), including the sitting Rector and half the Major Council. The rebuild was directed from Rome by Stjepan Gradić (1613–1683) , the Ragusan Vatican librarian and diplomat who raised funds across Europe and enforced a uniform Baroque rhythm along the Stradun. Every facade rises to the same cornice, every window aligns across 300 metres — this is regulation. The Sponza Palace, finished in 1522, survived the quake and is now also the war memorial. Where Old Town · Stradun · Sponza Palace

culture:Festa Sv. Vlaha · St Blaise Day.name: Festa Sv. Vlaha · St Blaise Day 3 February
culture:Festa Sv. Vlaha · St Blaise Day.label: UNESCO ICH 2009
culture:Festa Sv. Vlaha · St Blaise Day.hook: City's birthday · šporki makaruli on every Old Town menu
culture:Festa Sv. Vlaha · St Blaise Day.text: City's birthday · šporki makaruli on every Old Town menu Free (procession + church) ANNUAL Procession ~10:00, all-day open church The patron-saint feast since 972 AD , when St Blaise was said to have appeared to the priest Stojko to warn of an imminent Venetian sneak attack. On the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list since 2009. The procession passes down Stradun; relics from the cathedral are carried; the Rector — once one man for one month, now a ceremonial role — leads the city. The food window is the entire 31 January – 4 February week : ~19 Old Town restaurants run unified šporki makaruli menus. Where Old Town · St Blaise's Church · Stradun

culture:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 J.name: Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Jul – 25 Aug 2026
culture:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 J.label: 77TH EDITION 2026
culture:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 J.hook: Open with Libertas flag at 21:00 · close with Hamlet's final act
culture:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 J.text: Open with Libertas flag at 21:00 · close with Hamlet's final act EUR 25–95 / event BOOK-AHEAD Evenings The Festival began in 1950 and runs annually for 47 days, 10 July to 25 August in 2026 . The opening ceremony at 21:00 raises the LIBERTAS flag at St Blaise's Church and reads from Gundulić's Dubravka (1628). Hamlet at Lovrijenac , staged on the 37 m sea-fort since 1952, is the signature event — the rock fortress doubling for Elsinore. The Rector's Palace courtyard hosts chamber concerts; Sponza, the major orchestral programme; Fort Revelin, modern dance. Book three to four months ahead for the Hamlet performances. Where Lovrijenac · Rector's Palace · Sponza · Fort Revelin

culture:Memorial Room of the Defenders ·.name: Memorial Room of the Defenders · Sponza Palace
culture:Memorial Room of the Defenders ·.hook: Photographs of the dead · the quietest room in the city
culture:Memorial Room of the Defenders ·.text: Photographs of the dead · the quietest room in the city Free WALK-IN Late afternoon The Yugoslav People's Army siege ran 1 October 1991 to late May 1992 . The defining bombardment was 6 December 1991 : 19 civilians killed in a single day, 60 wounded, ~68% of Old Town buildings damaged. Total siege civilian deaths ~116; 194 Croatian defenders + 165 JNA fatalities. UNESCO placed Dubrovnik on the List of World Heritage in Danger and led the post-war restoration mission. The Memorial Room of the Defenders inside the Sponza Palace courtyard wing is the city's archive — photographs of the dead defenders, their ages and units, in two rooms of silence. Walk through after the cathedral; leave a moment of attention. Where Old Town · Sponza Palace

culture:Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551.name: Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551
culture:Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551.label: PLAYWRIGHT 1508–1567
culture:Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551.hook: Capon-with-oranges recipe still served at Kopun (Poljana Boškovića)
culture:Marin Držić · Dundo Maroje 1551.text: Capon-with-oranges recipe still served at Kopun (Poljana Boškovića) EUR 8 (House Museum) OPEN ALL YEAR Late morning Marin Držić (1508–1567) is the Renaissance playwright Croatia names before any other. His comedy Dundo Maroje (1551) premiered in the Rector's Palace and is still staged at the Summer Festival. The House Museum at Široka 7 in the Old Town reconstructs his working life through period interiors and manuscript facsimiles. The Držić recipe for capon with oranges, salt and honey is the dish on the menu at Kopun — the same lane, same square as the playwright walked four and a half centuries ago. Where Old Town · Široka 7 (House Museum)

culture:Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic.name: Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic-precursor theory
culture:Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic.label: POLYMATH 1711–1787
culture:Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic.hook: Boškovićeva Stairs = Game of Thrones Walk of Shame; physics history under the same flagstones
culture:Ruđer Bošković · the 1758 atomic.text: Boškovićeva Stairs = Game of Thrones Walk of Shame; physics history under the same flagstones Free WALK Any Ruđer Josip Bošković (1711–1787) , born in the Old Town, Jesuit polymath: astronomer, mathematician, physicist, diplomat. His Theoria Philosophiae Naturalis (Vienna 1758; Venice 1763) proposed matter as point-particles bound by mutual forces of attraction and repulsion — a precursor of atomic and field theory that Werner Heisenberg called "the Croatian Leibniz." Member of the Royal Society, the Académie Royale and the Russian Academy. Buried in Milan. The square at the foot of the Jesuit Stairs — Poljana Ruđera Boškovića — carries his name; the same stairs serve as the Game of Thrones Walk of Shame and as physics history under the same flagstones. Where Old Town · Poljana Ruđera Boškovića (Jesuit Stairs)

work:Cogito Coffee Gruž.name: Cogito Coffee Gruž
work:Cogito Coffee Gruž.label: ESPRESSO
work:Cogito Coffee Gruž.hook: The Zagreb specialty-coffee chain · best espresso in the city
work:Cogito Coffee Gruž.text: The Zagreb specialty-coffee chain · best espresso in the city Croatia's best specialty roaster. Long bench, fast Wi-Fi, sane noise level. Walking distance from ACI Marina. Decent flat white, single-origin pours, the occasional cardamom bun on the counter. Open 07:30–17:00 Mon–Sat. Where Gruž · Obala Stjepana Radića 21

work:Mara's Bar.name: Mara's Bar
work:Mara's Bar.label: WIFI
work:Mara's Bar.hook: Stable Wi-Fi inside the walls · charging plugs · breakfast all day
work:Mara's Bar.text: Stable Wi-Fi inside the walls · charging plugs · breakfast all day Small Old Town café with reliable Wi-Fi and plug points — rare combination inside the walls. Coffee + croissant + computer for two hours without anyone leaning on you. Owner Marija is the right kind of strict about who hogs the corner banquette. Where Old Town · Ulica Iza Roka

work:Mlinar Lapad.name: Mlinar Lapad
work:Mlinar Lapad.label: QUIET
work:Mlinar Lapad.hook: Bakery + quiet corner · cheap, cold-brew, AC in August
work:Mlinar Lapad.text: Bakery + quiet corner · cheap, cold-brew, AC in August Bakery chain — but the Lapad branch has a quiet upstairs corner with AC, fast Wi-Fi and a cold-brew tap. The croissants are honest, the burek is fast, the tables turn over more slowly than the Stradun cafés. Where Lapad · Kralja Tomislava strip

work:ACI Marina lounge.name: ACI Marina lounge
work:ACI Marina lounge.label: MARINA
work:ACI Marina lounge.hook: Marina-residents lounge · the right space for crew prep
work:ACI Marina lounge.text: Marina-residents lounge · the right space for crew prep The marina's resident lounge has Wi-Fi, AC, charging, and a coffee bar. Quiet weekday mornings. Available to ACI cardholders and yachts berthed in the marina; if you are working off a boat at Gruž, this is the prep room. Where Gruž · ACI Marina Dubrovnik

work:Rixos Libertas lobby.name: Rixos Libertas lobby
work:Rixos Libertas lobby.label: LOBBY
work:Rixos Libertas lobby.hook: Hotel lobby · solid Wi-Fi · sea view · order a coffee to earn the seat
work:Rixos Libertas lobby.text: Hotel lobby · solid Wi-Fi · sea view · order a coffee to earn the seat Five-star lobby that tolerates working guests if you order. Wi-Fi, sea view, AC, the right level of background hush. The hotel is 5 min walk above Pile Gate; useful for crew calls that need 90 minutes of quiet before service. Where Pile · Liechtensteinov Put 3

events:Festa Sv. Vlaha — St Blaise Day 2.name: Festa Sv. Vlaha — St Blaise Day 2026
events:Festa Sv. Vlaha — St Blaise Day 2.label: FEAST
events:Festa Sv. Vlaha — St Blaise Day 2.hook: 3 February 2026 · UNESCO ICH · 19 Old Town kitchens run a šporki menu
events:Festa Sv. Vlaha — St Blaise Day 2.text: 3 February 2026 · UNESCO ICH · 19 Old Town kitchens run a šporki menu The city's birthday and the only date in the year when ~19 Old Town restaurants run the unified šporki makaruli menu (the official list goes up at tzdubrovnik.hr in late January). Procession at 10:00 down Stradun; cathedral relics carried by Antunini; Rector leads the column. February in Dubrovnik is cold, quiet, oyster-peak, and crowdless — the right week to come if cooking is the point.

events:Mali Ston oyster opening · 19 Mar.name: Mali Ston oyster opening · 19 March
events:Mali Ston oyster opening · 19 Mar.label: ST JOSEPH
events:Mali Ston oyster opening · 19 Mar.hook: Traditional St Joseph's Day opening of the eating season
events:Mali Ston oyster opening · 19 Mar.text: Traditional St Joseph's Day opening of the eating season St Joseph's Day (Sv. Josip), 19 March is the traditional opening day of the Mali Ston oyster eating season. Local oyster farms host open-bay tastings; Bota Šare and Vila Koruna set up dockside service through April–May. Peak season runs to early June . Pair with Korčula Pošip — Krajančić or Bire.

events:Easter procession in Konavle — 5.name: Easter procession in Konavle — 5 April 2026
events:Easter procession in Konavle — 5.label: EASTER 2026
events:Easter procession in Konavle — 5.hook: Traditional Konavle costume, Linđo dancing in churchyards
events:Easter procession in Konavle — 5.text: Traditional Konavle costume, Linđo dancing in churchyards Easter Sunday 2026 falls on 5 April . The Konavle villages (Čilipi, Pridvorje, Gruda) hold processions in full traditional Konavle dress — the women's embroidered silk-trimmed costume is one of the most distinct in Dalmatia. Linđo dancing in churchyards follows the church service. Konavoski Dvori and the agroturizam houses run special lamb-and-rolling-pin menus across the weekend.

events:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Ju.name: Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Jul – 25 Aug 2026
events:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Ju.label: 77TH
events:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Ju.hook: Hamlet at Lovrijenac (74th year) · 70+ events over 47 days
events:Dubrovnik Summer Festival · 10 Ju.text: Hamlet at Lovrijenac (74th year) · 70+ events over 47 days The 77th Dubrovnik Summer Festival opens at 21:00 on 10 July 2026 with the LIBERTAS flag raised at St Blaise's Church and the reading from Gundulić's Dubravka . Closes 25 August 2026 . Hamlet at Lovrijenac (since 1952) is the signature; expect the play to be staged across 6–8 evenings during the run. Programme published in early March; tickets open the same week. Hamlet sells out in 72 hours.

events:Good Food Festival · Oct 6–19 202.name: Good Food Festival · Oct 6–19 2026
events:Good Food Festival · Oct 6–19 202.label: TASTING TRAIL
events:Good Food Festival · Oct 6–19 202.hook: Fixed-price tasting trails through 50+ city + Konavle restaurants
events:Good Food Festival · Oct 6–19 202.text: Fixed-price tasting trails through 50+ city + Konavle restaurants Dubrovnik's autumn food festival: 50+ restaurants in the city, Župa and Konavle run fixed-price tasting trails (a glass of wine + a small plate for EUR 5–10 per stop) across roughly 6–19 October 2026 . The Deša workshops on Stradun host pasta and pasticada demonstrations; oyster boats from Mali Ston tie up at the Old Port for shucking sessions. The thinking-chef's alternative to a midsummer trip — autumn light, cooler kitchens, no cruise crush.

events:New olive oil + new pršut · Novem.name: New olive oil + new pršut · November
events:New olive oil + new pršut · Novem.label: HARVEST
events:New olive oil + new pršut · Novem.text: Konavle agroturizam tastings · provisioning window New olive oil is pressed mid-October in Konavle and across Pelješac; by November it has clarified enough to bottle. The pršut hangs cured in the Drniš caves from late November. Konavle agroturizam houses run tastings across the month — Konoba Vinica Monković, Konoba Vinica Maraš, Konavle Cottages. This is the right provisioning window for the boat: small estates sell direct, 20-litre jerricans, lemons by the crate, late figs.

events:Dubrovnik Winter Festival · 29 No.name: Dubrovnik Winter Festival · 29 Nov 2025 – 3 Jan 2026 (annual)
events:Dubrovnik Winter Festival · 29 No.label: ADVENT
events:Dubrovnik Winter Festival · 29 No.hook: Christmas market on Stradun · 2025 opened with Doris Dragović
events:Dubrovnik Winter Festival · 29 No.text: Christmas market on Stradun · 2025 opened with Doris Dragović Annual winter festival on Luža Square, Stradun and Lapad — Christmas market, ice rinks, kuhano vino (mulled red), and free concerts. The 2025 edition opened with Doris Dragović on Stradun. The next edition will run roughly 28 Nov 2026 – 3 Jan 2027 . Winter is when locals reclaim the Old Town — cruise season is over, oyster season is back on, and zelena menestra is on every menu.

events:Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa.name: Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa · mid-July to mid-August
events:Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa.label: KLAPA
events:Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa.hook: 60th edition in 2026 · the national klapa competition
events:Omiš Festival of Dalmatian Klapa.text: 60th edition in 2026 · the national klapa competition Not strictly Dubrovnik — the Omiš Festival runs at the mouth of the Cetina river in Omiš (~3 h up the coast). But it is the national klapa championship , ongoing since 1967 and reaching its 60th edition in 2026 . Competing klapas often pass through Dubrovnik before or after; expect klapa concerts in the Old Town churches and at Lazareti through the same weeks (mid-July to mid-August). If a chef wants to understand klapa as a tradition rather than tourist soundtrack, Omiš is the source.

walks:City Walls loop.name: City Walls loop
walks:City Walls loop.text: The full ring: Pile entry → up the Bokar bastion → south wall sea-side → Minčeta (25 m, highest point) → back down to Pile. Stone reads 38–42 °C in full sun; no shade on the second half. EUR 35 combined ticket with Lovrijenac, EUR 25 walls only. Buy at the Pile booth or online to skip the first 20 min.

walks:Mount Srđ cable car + Fort Imperia.name: Mount Srđ cable car + Fort Imperial
walks:Mount Srđ cable car + Fort Imperia.text: The cable car climbs from above Buža 412 m to the summit of Srđ (3 min). Fort Imperial (Napoleon 1812) houses the Museum of Croatian War of Independence — the city's siege story, told from the mountain that the defenders held. Restaurant Panorama for a sunset drink. EUR 27 return .

walks:Lokrum island circuit.name: Lokrum island circuit
walks:Lokrum island circuit.text: Ferries leave the Old Port every 30 min from 09:00 (Easter to November, 12-min crossing, ~EUR 27 return incl. island entry). Walk: Benedictine monastery ruin → Maximilian's villa + Botanical Garden → Mrtvo More (small salt lake, swimmable) → southern cliffs. Picnic — no restaurants on the island. The Game of Thrones Iron Throne replica sits in the monastery cloister.

walks:Stradun five-squares walk.name: Stradun five-squares walk
walks:Stradun five-squares walk.text: Pile (Onofrio's fountain, 1438) → small Onofrio's fountain in Luža Square (Sponza + St Blaise's Church + Bell Tower + Orlando's Column 1418) → Gundulić Square (morning market, statue of Ivan Gundulić by Frangeš-Mihanović 1893) → Poljana Boškovića (Jesuit Stairs + St Ignatius) → Bunić (the Old Port view, with Lokrum on the horizon). Walk it before 09:00. The Stradun limestone is polished perilously slick in rain.

walks:Konavle Ljuta river + watermills w.name: Konavle Ljuta river + watermills walk
walks:Konavle Ljuta river + watermills w.text: Drive 35 min south to the Ljuta river in Konavle. Walk upstream from Konavoski Dvori through the watermills (some still grind in autumn). The river is cold-spring fed; air drops 5 °C beside the channel. Lunch at Konoba Konavoski Dvori — frog brodet, trout, lamb peka.

walks:Ston walls walk + salt pans.name: Ston walls walk + salt pans
walks:Ston walls walk + salt pans.text: Begun 1333 when Ston joined the Republic. 5.5 km — the longest stone defensive walls in Europe still standing. The walk climbs sharply over the Stonsko polje saddle to Mali Ston on the bay side. The Ston salt pans below (still in production after 4,000 years; harvest by hand July–September) supplied the Republic's salt monopoly. Combine with oyster lunch at Bota Šare.

walks:Cavtat harbour + Račić mausoleum.name: Cavtat harbour + Račić mausoleum
walks:Cavtat harbour + Račić mausoleum.text: 17 km south of Dubrovnik (tender 40 min or car 30 min). Walk the harbour past the Vlaho Bukovac House (1855–1922 painter, born here) to the Mestrović-built Račić Mausoleum on the cemetery peninsula — Ivan Meštrović 1922, full white marble. Stop at Galerija Vlaho Bukovac (EUR 6) on the way back. Konoba Galija for the dinner.

secret-gems:Buža — the hole-in-the-wall.name: Buža — the hole-in-the-wall bar
secret-gems:Buža — the hole-in-the-wall.label: GEM
secret-gems:Buža — the hole-in-the-wall.text: Two bars literally cut into the south sea wall — Buža means "hole." Walk past the cathedral down toward the wall, look for a small wooden door painted with "COLD DRINKS WITH THE MOST BEAUTIFUL VIEW." Tables on rocks above 10 m of water; swimmers jumping below. Drinks only — no food. Buža I and Buža II are run by different families; both honest. Beer + house white. Cash-only by tradition. Where Old Town · south sea wall When Daily 09:00 till after midnight in summer

secret-gems:Lazareti — the 1627 quaranti.name: Lazareti — the 1627 quarantine, now culture
secret-gems:Lazareti — the 1627 quaranti.label: GEM
secret-gems:Lazareti — the 1627 quaranti.text: The Lazareti were the city's 17th-c. plague quarantine — 10 stone halls along the shore , completed 1627, where merchants and goods waited 40 days before entering the city. Now they house the Linđo Folklore Ensemble 's summer performances, an art-house cinema and a programme of small concerts. The Stari Mlin restaurant occupies one hall in season. Walk through after the cable-car descent. Where Ploče · just outside the gate When Linđo summer Mon/Tue/Sat 21:30

secret-gems:Sokol Grad — the Konavle fal.name: Sokol Grad — the Konavle falcon fortress
secret-gems:Sokol Grad — the Konavle fal.label: GEM
secret-gems:Sokol Grad — the Konavle fal.text: First mentioned 1373; gifted to the Republic in 1391 by the Sanković family; abandoned after a 1672 earthquake; restored in 2013 . The largest Republic fortress outside the city. Perched on a 25 m vertical rock above Dunave village, 40 min south of Dubrovnik. Tiny museum inside; nearly always empty. EUR 8. Combine with lunch at Konavoski Dvori 30 min away. Where Dunave village · Konavle When Apr–Oct 10:00–19:00 / Nov–Mar 10:00–14:00

ethnic-restaurants:Asia Shop Dubrovnik.name: Asia Shop Dubrovnik
ethnic-restaurants:Asia Shop Dubrovnik.label: ASIAN
ethnic-restaurants:Asia Shop Dubrovnik.text: The serviceable Asian grocer of the city — soy, mirin, gochujang, sushi rice, nori, rice vinegars, Thai curries, kecap manis. Stock changes; call ahead for specific items. The one address a charter kitchen needs for a Japanese guest request. Where Lapad · Iva Vojnovića 32

ethnic-restaurants:Konzum on Gundulićeva.name: Konzum on Gundulićeva Poljana
ethnic-restaurants:Konzum on Gundulićeva.label: SUPERMARKET
ethnic-restaurants:Konzum on Gundulićeva.text: The supermarket Old-Town locals actually use — sane prices on bottled water (3–5× cheaper than Stradun café markups), Croatian basics, the Dolcela baking shelf, and the reliable Vegeta-and-Podravka aisle for Balkan pantry classics. Where Pile · just outside the gate

street-food:Burek (cheese / spinach / me.name: Burek (cheese / spinach / meat phyllo)
street-food:Burek (cheese / spinach / me.label: BAKERY
street-food:Burek (cheese / spinach / me.text: Burek — flaky phyllo coil filled with cheese, spinach or minced meat — is the Balkan breakfast and the Croatian school-pickup snack. The Mlinar chain bakes decent versions to 11:00; Pekara Bobi at Gruž does denser, more home-style coils. Eat hot ; cold burek is sad. With a small Karlovačko or a Niksicko, EUR 4–6. Where Mlinar bakery on Lapad strip · also Pekara Bobi at Gruž

street-food:Ćevapi at Taj Mahal (the Bos.name: Ćevapi at Taj Mahal (the Bosnian one, not Indian)
street-food:Ćevapi at Taj Mahal (the Bos.label: GRILL
street-food:Ćevapi at Taj Mahal (the Bos.text: Despite the name, Taj Mahal is a Bosnian grill — ćevapi (minced-meat fingers, char-grilled, served in lepinja flatbread with raw onion and ajvar) the right way. Also klepe, sogan dolma, the burek. The owner is from Sarajevo; the menu is honest Balkan, not theme-park. EUR 15–22 pp. Where Old Town · Nikole Gučetića

burger-kebab:Barba — \"slow Dalmatian fa.name: Barba — "slow Dalmatian fast food"
burger-kebab:Barba — \"slow Dalmatian fa.label: STREET
burger-kebab:Barba — \"slow Dalmatian fa.text: Octopus burger, mahi-mahi taco, salted-cod croquettes — Adriatic fish in fast-food formats. The octopus burger is the order. Counter and 6 tables. EUR 12–18 pp, walk-in. Where Old Town · Boškovićeva 5

burger-kebab:Mirakul Burger — Lapad.name: Mirakul Burger — Lapad
burger-kebab:Mirakul Burger — Lapad.label: STREET
burger-kebab:Mirakul Burger — Lapad.text: Smash burger in the American style with Croatian beef, brioche bun, sharp pickle, house pravi-sir cheese. Tucked into the Lapad pedestrian strip. EUR 12–17 pp, ordered at the counter. Where Lapad · Iva Dulčića 5

gastronomy:Gruž Market (Tržnica Gruž).name: Gruž Market (Tržnica Gruž)
gastronomy:Gruž Market (Tržnica Gruž).text: The provisioning market for the boat. Walk 8 minutes from ACI Marina Dubrovnik. Scorpionfish, sea bream, John Dory, monkfish off the morning boats; octopus, cuttlefish, the day's prawns. Outdoor: tomato, fig, olive oil mandolins, Konavle cheese. Cash strongly preferred . Mondays quiet, Tuesday–Saturday is the run. Address Obala Stjepana Radića, Gruž

gastronomy:Gundulićeva Poljana — Old Tow.name: Gundulićeva Poljana — Old Town morning market
gastronomy:Gundulićeva Poljana — Old Tow.text: The Old Town morning market under Gundulić's statue (Frangeš-Mihanović 1893). Closes early — by 14:00 the stalls fold. Best for: candied bitter-orange peel (arancini, the Dubrovnik confection), lavender from Hvar, dried figs, herb bunches, and the cold-pressed olive oils in glass bottles. Smaller than Gruž, more touristed; less for fish, better for confections to take back to the boat. Address Gundulić Square, Old Town

gastronomy:Mali Ston quay (oysters direc.name: Mali Ston quay (oysters direct)
gastronomy:Mali Ston quay (oysters direc.text: Not a market in the formal sense — but the oyster boats from the bay tie up at the Mali Ston quay through the season and sell oysters and mussels directly. Bring a clean basket, ice, and small bills. The Bota Šare farm has a fixed dock stall most mornings; ask at the restaurant if no one is at the quay. PDO 2020/1469 Ostrea edulis at zero kilometres. Address Mali Ston waterfront, Pelješac

gastronomy:Grgić Vina — Trstenik, Pelješ.name: Grgić Vina — Trstenik, Pelješac
gastronomy:Grgić Vina — Trstenik, Pelješ.text: Mike Grgich's homecoming winery. Two wines only, every year: Plavac Mali (multi-vintage Dingač-style) and Pošip (Korčula). Tasting room at Trstenik on the south shore of Pelješac. Mike Grgich died 2023; daughter Violet and nephew Ivo Jeramaz run the estate. Tasting EUR 25–45 pp by appointment.

gastronomy:Miloš Stagnum — Ponikve, Pelj.name: Miloš Stagnum — Ponikve, Pelješac
gastronomy:Miloš Stagnum — Ponikve, Pelj.text: Frano Miloš at Ponikve, on south-facing 150–250 m slopes. 15 ha organic, wild-yeast fermentation, three years in old Slavonian oak. Hugh Johnson called the 1993 Stagnum "Croatia's first cult wine." Frano personally pours; appointment only. The Stagnum top cuvée is the wine to bring back to the boat.

gastronomy:Mali Ston Bay oyster farms (c.name: Mali Ston Bay oyster farms (collective)
gastronomy:Mali Ston Bay oyster farms (c.text: The oyster collective of the Mali Ston Bay — small family farms (Bota Šare, Pelješki Sušac, Drače) holding the PDO since the 6 October 2020 EU registration. Peak season March to May; opening day St Joseph 19 March. About 90% of Croatian oyster production. Buy at quay or at the restaurants — the cost-of-living index for the bay is the per-oyster price (EUR 2.50–4 dockside).

gastronomy:Saints Hills — Oskorušno, Pel.name: Saints Hills — Oskorušno, Pelješac + Komarna
gastronomy:Saints Hills — Oskorušno, Pel.text: The Tolj family estate with the Rolland consulting badge. Flagships: Sv. Lucija Dingač and Sv. Roko Komarna. Also Istrian whites (Mala Nevina). Open tasting room with food pairing; one of the easier Pelješac visits to book.

gastronomy:Maraska d.d. — Zadar.name: Maraska d.d. — Zadar
gastronomy:Maraska d.d. — Zadar.text: Maraska d.d. (founded 1946) consolidated the historic Zadar maraschino producers after the war. The Marasca cherry was brought from Asia Minor in Roman times; Dominican monks perfected the liqueur in the 16th c.; Francesco Drioli industrialized in 1759. The liqueur was on the first-class drinks list of the Titanic in 1912. Distillery tours by appointment in Zadar; the bottles are everywhere in Dalmatia.

gastronomy:Franciscan Monastery Pharmacy.name: Franciscan Monastery Pharmacy (1317)
gastronomy:Franciscan Monastery Pharmacy.text: Founded 1317; the third-oldest pharmacy in the world counting non-continuous operations, and the oldest still-operating one in Europe . Sells rose creams, sage soaps, almond oils and pine balms made from the friars' historical recipes. The shop is at the front of the Monastery; the museum-pharmacy hall behind (EUR 6 entry) preserves the 14th-c. apothecary. Address Stradun 2, Old Town

gastronomy:Dežo Art (Konavle textiles).name: Dežo Art (Konavle textiles)
gastronomy:Dežo Art (Konavle textiles).text: Hand-embroidered Konavle textiles — the silk-trimmed costume worn in the Easter procession is the most distinct in Dalmatia. Aprons, scarves, the traditional oglavlje head-piece. Real Konavle work, not mass print. Ask for Lela; she will explain the stitch families. Address Dropčev prolaz, Old Town

gastronomy:Uje — Croatian olive oils.name: Uje — Croatian olive oils
gastronomy:Uje — Croatian olive oils.text: The Uje brand selects from Croatian estates — Istrian and Dalmatian. The Konavle oils (smaller estates than the famous Istrian ones, but very respectable) and the Korčula oils are the ones to bring back. Salt-flake selections from the Ston pans; rakija pours by the small bottle. Tasting flights at the back. Address Placa 5, Old Town

avoid:Prijeko Street tourist traps.name: Prijeko Street tourist traps
avoid:Prijeko Street tourist traps.text: Menus in 8–10 languages · touts on the street · frozen fish under "fresh" signs

avoid:Reheated pizza on Stradun.name: Reheated pizza on Stradun
avoid:Reheated pizza on Stradun.text: Frozen base, microwaved, EUR 18–22 a slice in the touristed mid-Stradun cafés

avoid:\"Fresh\" oyster claims inside the.name: "Fresh" oyster claims inside the walls
avoid:\"Fresh\" oyster claims inside the.text: Oysters travel 1 h 30 from Mali Ston by road; in shoulder season they may be 3–4 days old

avoid:Truffle products in Dubrovnik.name: Truffle products in Dubrovnik
avoid:Truffle products in Dubrovnik.text: Truffle is an Istrian product, not a Dubrovnik one — what you find here is imported or oil-flavoured
